reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis contains a critical physical contradiction: low stacking fault energy (SFE) inhibits cross-slip, not facilitates it, so the proposed mechanism of low SFE enabling extensive cross-slip and rapid dynamic recovery is fundamentally wrong.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is detailed and could be executed, but it is designed to verify a physically incorrect mechanism, so even a well-executed test would not properly evaluate the true cause of the low hardness.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it is built on a flawed understanding of stacking fault energy and cross-slip, which would misdirect research efforts and waste resources.
